item.title: Browser Setu 0.3.3
item.description:
Mac: notarized DMG. iPhone/iPad: TestFlight build 19. Same version, higher build number.
## Fixed: windows (Mac) - **A link opened from another app no longer makes a new window.** Click Sign in in the Claude app, a link in Mail or a chat, and it opens as a **tab in the window in front**. Before, it opened a new window holding a blank "New Tab" beside the link's tab. - **Quit and open again no longer multiplies windows.** macOS was restoring the windows and the app was restoring them too, so the count grew at every start. Your windows now come back once, each with its own tabs (at most 8 extra). - A Dock click with no window opens one window. Quitting is no longer treated as you closing windows. - Checked on the real app: three quit-and-open cycles and links sent with the app closed, open, and twice in a row all left the same number of windows.
## Fixed: tabs - **A tab opened from a page** (a link, ⌘-click, a script) now sits **next to the tab that opened it**, like Chrome and Firefox. Several background tabs keep the order they were opened in. A New Tab still goes to the end, and pinned tabs stay first. - **Closing the selected tab** brings forward the tab on its right (the one on its left if it was last), or **the tab it was opened from** if you have not looked at anything else since. Before, the wrong neighbour could come forward when other workspaces or groups held tabs.
## iPhone - Landscape bar: a **New Tab** button and a centred address field, like Safari on its side.
## Also - How each window and tab action behaves, with its sources, is in `docs/windows.md`. - New tests for the window rules and the tab rules.
## Not changed - Control-Tab does not switch tabs yet. - A window's pop-ups (a sign-in box) still open as tabs joined to their page, not as small windows.

item.title: Browser Setu 0.3.3
item.description:
Mac: notarized DMG. iPhone/iPad: TestFlight build 18. Same version, higher build number.
## Added - **AI features switch** (Settings › AI): one switch that turns off page summaries, Ask This Page and the AI-tool connection. - **Use Browser Setu from AI tools and scripts** (downloadable Mac build only, off by default): a local Model Context Protocol connection for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor and others, and a `bsetu` shell script. You share tabs, allow sites, and are asked before most buttons are pressed, most typing, and anything that sends, pays or deletes. - **Coming from another browser** table in the README.
## Safety rules for AI tools (checked in review) - What is typed into a field is never read. - Addresses are shown without query, fragment or token-like pieces. - A tab is read only on an allowed website; links to other sites ask first. - Typing asks unless it is a plain search box; most buttons ask. - Stop cuts every connection and cancels what is under way; a new token ends the old one at once. - At most 8 connections; a client that sends nothing in 10 seconds is dropped.
## Also in this build - **Settings › AI** is its own panel in the Mac sidebar (under Browser). Clear Everything Now and the look-alike warning are under Privacy & Security; time rules are under Tabs. Settings search finds all of them. - **Tools menu** everywhere (iPhone menu, iPad ⋮ menu, Mac menu bar, new tab page): Daily Digest, Feeds / Tasks / Vault / Clipboard, Reading List, Screenshot and Mark Up, Reopen My Last Session, Watch This Page, Privacy Grade, All Commands, Clear Everything Now. - **Plain-word history search** in the normal address bar ("pasta recipe last week"). - Every link an AI tool follows asks first unless you turn that off; Return asks except in a search box; typed text is never written to the activity log; shared tabs are found in every window; a dropped or stopped request cancels its work; tool arguments are checked before the browser sees them. - Card numbers, US social security numbers and IBANs are masked in page text. Names, emails, addresses, birth dates and other account numbers are not, and the documentation says so.
## Know before you use it - The AI-tool connection is in the **downloadable Mac build only**. The App Store build and iPhone/iPad have the master AI switch but no tool connection. - It has been tested with unit tests and a real-socket test, not yet with a real AI tool in daily use.

item.title: Browser Setu 0.3.3
item.description:
Mac: notarized DMG. iPhone/iPad: TestFlight build 16. Same version, higher build number.
## Added since build 15 - **Look-alike address warning:** pages that imitate a well-known site are held back until you choose to continue. - **Privacy grade (A to F)** for the page in front, with reasons, in *This site…*; per-site zoom, light or dark look, private-tab rule and permission "Take Back" in the same place. - **Clear Everything Now:** one confirmed step that closes all tabs and erases history, data, copied text and the shared inbox. - **Daily Digest:** reading list, feeds, tasks and time on sites in one list. - **Automatic switching:** time rules that move to a workspace as their time begins (Mac). - **Ask in plain words:** "pasta recipe last week" finds it in history from the command palette. - **Tab groups travel** between devices; the sleeping-tab moon and reason. - **Mac Share menu entry** (App Store build) and the iPhone/iPad share sheet. - **Control Center and Lock Screen buttons** (iOS 18) and redrawn widgets. - **Mac menu-bar search hotkey:** Control-Option-Space. - **Link previews** on press-and-hold.
## Fixed - iPhone and iPad now register the `browsersetu://` link scheme. Before this, widget taps, Control Center buttons and Shortcuts links did not open the app. - Accent colour stays as chosen when a theme changes; density changes the iPhone address bar height. - Removing a profile retries until WebKit has released its data. - The browser's own scroll-restore scripts run in an isolated world.

item.title: Browser Setu 0.3.3
item.description:
# Browser Setu 0.3.3 (build 11)
Mac: notarized, stapled DMG (replaces the build 10 file on the same release). iPhone/iPad: TestFlight build 11. Same version number, higher build number.
## Added since build 10 - **iPad has its own touch design:** a one-row toolbar, large tab chips, a redrawn tab overview, the iPhone's full menu in ⋮, panels docked beside the page, a scroll-away toolbar with a return pill, and external-keyboard shortcuts. - **Library panels** (Bookmarks, History, Downloads): beside the page, as a tab, or as a floating card, chosen in Settings or the first-run setup; the Mac sidebar's Downloads button now opens the panel instead of swapping the tab list. - **First-run setup explains every choice in plain words** and has a new step for where the panels open. - **Two-step sign-ins:** a saved username is filled on the first step (silently when only one is saved), the password on the next step behind Touch ID or Face ID. - Settings window: no system title; the panel's own header names the page. Rows in History are one line. Lists load before they show, so rows no longer appear loose and then regroup.
## Fixed - iPad ⌘L and ⌘K did nothing (they opened the phone's floating panel); now they focus the address field. - The floating card no longer leaves an empty area under a short list. - `try!` regex initialisers replaced by a safe fallback; documented the startup stop and the plain-HTTP web-content setting; CI now runs the fuzz tests and the SBOM script.
## Checked - Full Mac unit run: 574 passed, 7 failed. Six of the failures were timing and scale tests that took 15 to 25 minutes after about 500 earlier tests had left web views behind (opening 100 tabs took 25 minutes); each passed when run alone (opening 100 tabs took 0.5 seconds). The seventh, a check that the running app is sandboxed with the right entitlements, can only pass in a signed build and was not run signed. - Earlier, 12 focused suites (login, username step, privacy, fuzz, shortcuts, layout, page versions, YouTube rules) passed.
## Not checked - iPhone and iPad unit and UI tests; the iPad design on a real iPad with an external keyboard (Safari failed on that keyboard too, so the cause may be the iPad or keyboard); live sign-ins and YouTube; real two-device sync; VoiceOver; the signed-build sandbox test.

item.title: Browser Setu 0.2.0
item.description: First public release. A native WebKit browser for macOS with a Rust core: tabs, sidebar layouts, workspaces, content blocking, per-site privacy, saved passwords in your Keychain, web extensions, research collections, developer tools, and automatic updates.
